item.title: MANGO extends free membership through March
item.description: (MANGO) — The Marianas Alliance of Non-Governmental Organizations has announced an extension of free membership through March as it prepares to transition to a new membership structure designed to support long-term sustainability and strengthen the nonprofit sector. The post MANGO extends free membership through March appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Shop local this Valentine’s season at ‘Love Local’ pop-up market
item.description: (NMC-SBDC) — The CNMI Innovation Incubator is proud to present Love Local, a Valentine’s-themed pop-up market highlighting the creativity and innovation of local entrepreneurs. The event will take place on Saturday, Feb. 7, 2026, from 4 p.m. to 7 p.m. in the Beach Road Plaza parking lot. The post Shop local this Valentine’s season at ‘Love Local’ pop-up market appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Solar lights for San Jose Church
item.description: Businessman Steve Jang, center, poses with parishioners of San Jose Church after donating three solar-powered lights on Saturday. “It’s a gift that keeps on giving,” Jang said, adding that the lights will lower operating costs, reduce the church’s environmental footprint, and allow more resources to directly benefit the community. “It’s about planting seeds of sustainability and generosity that will bear fruit long into the future,” he said. item.title: Industry Day at NMC
item.description: Military officials speak with local contractors during Industry Day, hosted by the CNMI Small Business Development Center at Northern Marianas College. The Industry Day sessions were held on Saipan, Tinian and Rota last week and focused on sharing updates, resources and opportunities related to federal and government contracting. item.title: Fake green cards lead to woman’s arrest
item.description: LORNA Maramba was arrested after U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers caught her using two falsified permanent resident cards to travel from the CNMI to Hawaii, according to a federal complaint unsealed last week. item.title: CNMI mourns passing of Carolinian cultural icon Lino Olopai
item.description: THE CNMI is mourning the loss of Lino Mettao “Tata Lino” Olopai, a revered Carolinian cultural leader, master navigator, and knowledge bearer who passed away peacefully on Thursday at the age of 86.
